title: Deceive Oneself
english_paragraphs: Once upon a time, a thief saw a beautiful, large bell and wanted to carry it home. But the bell was so big and heavy that he could only think of one way to take it: break it into pieces and carry them home separately.

The thief found a large hammer and struck the bell hard. It made a loud sound that gave him a fright. He threw his arms around the bell, trying to muffle the sound—but how could he? The thief grew anxious. Wasn’t the ringing telling everyone he was stealing the bell?

The more he listened, the more frightened he became. Without thinking, he covered his ears with his hands. “I can’t hear it anymore!” he said happily. He thought no one else could hear it either, so he plugged his ears with cloth and struck the bell again and again. Its loud ringing carried far and wide. When people heard it, they came running and caught the thief.

Once upon a time, a thief saw a beautiful, large bell and wanted to carry it home. But the bell was so big and heavy that he could only think of one way to take it: break it into pieces and carry them home separately.

The thief found a large hammer and struck the bell hard. It made a loud sound that gave him a fright. He threw his arms around the bell, trying to muffle the sound—but how could he? The thief grew anxious. Wasn’t the ringing telling everyone he was stealing the bell?

The more he listened, the more frightened he became. Without thinking, he covered his ears with his hands. “I can’t hear it anymore!” he said happily. He thought no one else could hear it either, so he plugged his ears with cloth and struck the bell again and again. Its loud ringing carried far and wide. When people heard it, they came running and caught the thief.
russian_paragraphs: Одна́жды вор уви́дел краси́вый большо́й ко́локол и зажа́л его́ нести́ до́ма. Но ко́локол был насто́лько большо́й и тяжёло́й, что он смо́г приду́мать только один спо́соб, как его взять: разби́ть его́ на кусо́чки и нести́ их до́ма отде́льно.

Вор нашёл большо́й мо́лот и сильно уда́рил ко́локол. Он издал гро́мкий звук, который испугал его́. Он обнял ко́локол, пыта́ясь заглуши́ть звук — но как он мог это сделать? Вор стал беспоко́йным. Разве зво́н не говори́л всем, что он кра́дёт ко́локол?

Чем больше он слу́шал, тем бо́льше он испуга́лся. Без мы́сли он закры́л свои́ у́ши рука́ми. “Я больше не слы́шу его́!” — сча́стливо ска́зал он. Он ду́мал, что никто́ другóй тоже не слы́шит, поэтому закле́ил у́ши тканью и удари́л по ко́локолу сно́ва и сно́ва. Его́ гро́мкий зво́н разнёсся по всему́ окрýжéнию. Когда люди́ услы́шали его́, они при́бегали и поймали вора.
reading_paragraphs: Odnázhdy vor uvíděl krásivý bol'shóy kólokol i zhazhál egó nestí́ domóy. No kólokol byl nastól'ko bol'shóy i tyazhóly, chto on smóg pridumát' tol'ko odín spósob, kak ego vzyát': razbí́t' egó na kusóchki i nestí́ ikh domóy otdél'no.

Vor našél bol'shóy môlot i sil'no udaríl kólokol. On izdal gromký zvúkd, kotorýy ispugál yegó. On obnyál kólokol, pytáyas' zaglušit' zvúk — no kak on mog etó sdélat'? Vor stal bespokóynym. Razve zvón ne govoríl všem, chto on krádet kólokol?

Chém bol'she on slúshal, tém bólshe on ispugálsya. Bez mýsli on zakrýl svoí úshi rukámi. “Ya bol'she ne slýshu egó!” — schastlivo skázal on. On dômáal, chto niktó drugóy tozhe ne slýshit, poetomu zakléil úshi tkányu i udaríl po kólokolu snóva i snóva. Egó gromký zvón razniósya po vsemu okrúzhéru. Kogdá lyudí uslýshali egó, oni príbegali i poymali vora.
